title: AutoRole-Tiny
subtitle: Single-genome role differentiation for collective inference on MCU sensor swarms
summary: A decentralized TinyML system that enables homogeneous nRF52840 nodes to adapt sensing, relay, reporting, and sleep roles from local observations.
motivation: Homogeneous MCU swarms must adapt their responsibilities under changing sensing, communication, and energy conditions without centralized coordination.
problem: How can a single compact policy produce complementary node roles while remaining deployable on resource-constrained hardware?
method: Use fixed-size mailboxes and permutation-invariant neighbor aggregation, supported by a PyTorch-to-C++ INT8 deployment workflow.
results: Quantization consistency, latency, Flash/RAM use, and GPIO-triggered energy are being evaluated on physical nodes.

title: FireGuard
subtitle: Multimodal fire-risk early warning and intervention
status: Completed research project · Patent accepted by CNIPA
summary: A Jetson Nano and ESP32 system for multimodal fire-risk detection and intervention in underground electric-vehicle charging environments.
motivation: Early fire-risk signals are heterogeneous and difficult to identify reliably with a single sensing modality.
problem: How can thermal and environmental signals be combined for timely edge-assisted warning and intervention?
method: Fuse thermal, gas, and flame sensing in an edge-device architecture and evaluate distributed decisions through a hardware-in-the-loop testbed.
results: Completed with an Excellent rating under the National Undergraduate Innovation Program; produced a first-listed-inventor patent application.

title: Multimodal Driver Fatigue and Distraction Monitoring
subtitle: Multimodal driver-state understanding for transportation safety
status: Active project · Patent accepted by CNIPA
summary: A driver-state monitoring framework combining visual, audio and speech, and smoking-related gas or smoke cues.
motivation: Fatigue and distraction manifest differently across drivers and operating conditions, making single-modality systems brittle.
problem: How can heterogeneous in-cabin signals be verified over time and fused into practical graded warnings?
method: Combine temporal verification, risk-score fusion, and graded warning logic across visual, audio, and environmental signals.
results: Produced a Chinese invention patent application as second-listed co-inventor; fast pre-examination passed.

title: SAtom: Swarms as Tools for Object Manipulation
subtitle: Collective virtual end-effectors for feedback-driven swarm control
summary: A swarm manipulation system using collective virtual end-effectors for feedback-driven foundation-model control.
motivation: Robot swarms can act as reconfigurable physical tools for manipulation beyond the capability of individual agents.
problem: How can a foundation model command a swarm while physical feedback maintains accurate manipulation?
method: Construct collective virtual end-effectors and close the loop with physical feedback during object placement.
results: Achieved 89.2% success and 10.4 mm mean placement error across 120 physical trials.

title: RK3568 Edge Vision System for Oriented Fastener Inspection
subtitle: INT8 oriented-object detection on an embedded edge platform
summary: A 13-class YOLOv8s-OBB inspection system deployed with INT8 RKNN inference on QSM368ZP-WF/RK3568.
motivation: Industrial fastener inspection requires accurate orientation-aware detection under edge-computing constraints.
problem: How can an oriented detector retain accuracy after conversion and quantization for RK3568 deployment?
method: Build reproducible calibration, RKNN conversion, board testing, and log-audit tooling for deployment validation.
results: Achieved 99.1% mAP@50 and 94.7% mAP@50–95; audited hard cases across 20 inference logs.
artifacts: 9th National Embedded Chip and System Design Competition

title: LLM-Augmented Multi-Agent Emergency Evacuation Simulation
subtitle: Hazard-aware pedestrian decisions in EV charging garages
summary: A Unity/Tuanjie emergency simulation integrating thermal-runaway progression, intervention, and pedestrian evacuation.
motivation: Emergency evacuation decisions depend on local hazards and changing conditions that fixed scripts represent poorly.
problem: How can simulated pedestrians choose context-aware actions while remaining connected to navigation and state transitions?
method: Use an LLM-augmented multi-agent module to select actions from local hazards and drive Unity navigation and agent states.
results: Received First Prize in the 10th Central South University Virtual Simulation Design Competition.
